chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ribat, who narrated, saying:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'If a man from the People of the Book (dhimmi) converts to Islam, while his father is still alive, and his father has other children besides him; then when the father dies, the Muslim son inherits all of his father's wealth, and his father's other children and his wife do not inherit anything from him alongside the Muslim son.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.ذِمِّيّاً: A non-Muslim subject (specifically People of the Book)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of a non-Muslim father when his son converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *ikhtilaf al-millatayn* (difference in religion) as a complete barrier to inheritance, specifically highlighting the superior status of the Muslim son over his non-Muslim father. It establishes that the Muslim heir excludes all other relatives, including the father and the father's wife, from receiving any share of the estate, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice and affirmed by Shia jurists. This case illustrates the asymmetry in inheritance rights where a Muslim can inherit from a non-Muslim relative, but not vice versa.
